projects.title: Multi-Container WordPress Deployment
description: This DevOps project is a containerized WordPress blog platform built with Docker Compose, consisting of three containers: WordPress for content management, MariaDB for storing data and Nginx for serving the website.
During this project I learned to use Docker containers and link them toghether using Docker netwoks. How to build custom Docker images and automate deployment using Docker Compose.

projects.title: Custom IRC server
description: This team project is an Internet Relay Chat (IRC) server with essential features and multiple client connections.
An Internet Relay Chat or IRC is a text-based communication protocol on the internet, It offers real-time messaging that can be either public or private.
The project is implemented in C++ with the goal of learning how to implement a server, use sockets and handle client-server communication.

projects.title: Portfolio
description: This project is a personal portfolio website to showcase projects and skills. The website is built to be responsive and interactive with accessability in mind

During this project I learned how to build a website using TypeScript and React and to style it with Tailwind CSS. Developing the project also gave me the opportunity to learn how to deploy a website using Vercel!

projects.title: Raycasting game
description: This team project is a raycasting-based 3D game implemented in C, inspired by the world-famous Wolfenstein 3D game, which was the first ever FPS (Firs-Person Shooter) game!

During this project I my responsibility was to make a dynamic view inside a maze using the raycasting algorithm, based on a 2D grid map file. My teammates responsibility was to fill the shapes using textures, after which we both worked on player events

This not only taught me graphical programming in C and how to implement a raycasting algorithm, but most importantly how to work effectively in a team and utilize each others strenghts to make something we're all proud of!

projects.title: UNIX shell
description: This team project is a small UNIX shell which imitates the behavior of bash. The shell supports pipes, redirections, environment variable expansions, a few built-in commands and user keyboard signals.
The goal of this project is to learn how a UNIX shell works in a deeper level, how to parse input and execute shell commands in a seperate process in C

During this project my responsibility was to implement a few UNIX signal interpretations, building the supported built-in commands and executing commands, while handling child processes and file descriptors.

projects.title: The dining philosophers problem simulator
description: This project is a text-based simulation for the dining philosophers problem with a little twist of adding sleeping in the mix.
The dining philosophers problem is:

One or more philosophers sit around a round table. There is a large bowl of spaghetti in the middle of the table.
- The philosophers aternatively eat, think or sleep
- There are as many forks on the table as there are philosophers
- A philosopher can only eat their spaghetti when they have both their left and right fork
- When a philosopher has finished eating they put their forks back on the table and start sleeping. Once awake they start thinking again until they can start eating

The simulation stops when a philosopher dies of starvation
During this project I learned how to build a multitasking program using threads, use mutexes to ensure safety and to prevent data races and deadlocks

projects.title: 3D Map Visualizer
description: This project is a wireframe renderer that converts a 2D map into a 3D representation
During this project I learned the basics of computer graphics with the challenge of implementing trigonometry in C. How to visualize user events and create a clear UI.

projects.title: Number sorting algorithm
description: This project is program that sorts a stack of integers by using the minimal amount of actions using a second stack to store the sorted integers.
For this problem the algorithm that I implemented was The Turk Algoritm, which was the most efficient solution for this specific project.
During this project I learned the basics of algorithms and data structures and how to utilize them in the C language.
